To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the energy distribution at the cathode of the glow discharge depends on the nature of the cathode material, the nature of the gas, and the pressure.
the cathode of a glow discharge takes up about 80% of the cathode fall energy in H\({}_{2}\) and about 85% in N\({}_{2}+20\) Torr H\({}_{3}\)O vapor.
the energy distribution at the cathode of a hydrogen arc is not a function of the cathode material and that the cathode energy distribution is not a function only of the cathode temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of an energy-efficient and cost-effective system for the production of hydrogen by electrolysis.
the energy distribution at a cathode of a glow discharge.
the development and application of a new method for the determination of the energy distribution of the electrons in the negative glow of a glow discharge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the energy distribution of the electrons at the cathode of a glow discharge is determined by the following factors: * the energy of the cathode material; * the energy of ionization of the gas; * the energy loss of the cathode particles in the gas; * secondary electron emission; * the work function of the cathode; * the energy losses of the cathode electrons at the cathodic surface; * the energy distribution of electrons at the cathodal surface.
the cathode of a hydrogen discharge at room temperature takes up in the average, 80 per cent. of the cathode fall energy.
the cathode in an arc discharge takes up in the average, at room temperature, 80 percent of the cathode fall energy in the case of hydrogen, and about 85 percent in the case of nitrogen and steam.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cathode of an arc discharge is a sink for a large fraction of the arc energy.
the cathode energy spectrum is determined by the cathode material and the cathode surface temperature.

, in the presence of the catalyst, the energy distribution of electrons in the cathode of a glow discharge at room temperature is determined by the nature of the cathode material and of the working gas, and that the energy distribution is independent of the discharge current.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy distribution at the cathode of an electric discharge in mercury vapor is not uniform.
we have demonstrated the ability to control electron emission from the surface of a metal by tuning the work function of the metal.
the distribution of energy in the cathode sheath is not a constant, but depends on the plasma parameters.
